newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rothfos forecasts 96/97 coffee deficit, exports.
newsitem.headline: Rothfos forecasts 96/97 coffee deficit, exports.

text.p: Global coffee production in 1996/97 should reach 97.5 million bags and consumption 99 million, German trader Bernhard Rothfos GmbH said on Tuesday.

A Rothfos statement said the latest production figure was slightly below an October 1996 estimate of 97.6 million bags because an increase in robusta output was now expected to be further offset by a fall in arabica production.
Production in 1995/96 was untypically low at 86.6 million bags because of Brazil crop losses, according to Rothfos, the Hamburg-based trading company of Neumann Kaffee Gruppe.
Its global coffee exports estimate of 74.7 million bags in 96/97 compared with 74.8 million anticipated last October and exports of 73.2 million in the 95/96 year.
The latest figure implied additional stocks drawdowns in consuming countries of 300,000 bags in 96/97, Rothfos said.
It put consumer country stocks as of September 30, 1996, at 8.7 million bags and 96/97 consumption in these importing countries at 75.0 million bags.
There would be no room for stockbuilding and historically low levels of coverage -- which were down at six weeks' use on Sept 30, 1996 -- would continue throughout the coffee year.
Rothfos also said it had analysed likely consumption and exports according to coffee types and it had arrived at a three million bag deficit in arabicas in the 96/97 season.
This should continue to be reflected by the inverted structure of the New York C arabica market and a wide arbitrage between New York and London robusta futures.
